clue.text: Lobster perhaps reddish-brown: serve in tin

indicators.note: the colour and the serve are placed in the tin, which wraps round them

parts.note: a tin is a can
rust is a reddish-brown colour
an ace is an unreturnable serve in tennis

explanation.surface: Describing a lobster's colour, then telling the cook to serve it from a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serve' looks like an instruction to the cook, but it is the tennis ace.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobster is one example of a crustacean, a shelled marine animal; 'perhaps' flags the example.

clue.text: One theologian upset eating old Cypriot cheese

indicators.note: the overturned pair takes in a letter, as if eating it
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a mullah is a Muslim scholar of theology

explanation.surface: A religious scholar knocked over while scoffing some ancient cheese from Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns I MULLAH into HALLUMI, and 'eating' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloumi is a firm, salty grilling cheese traditionally made on Cyprus.

clue.text: Such sweet solutions could make us spry

indicators.note: these letters could be rearranged to make the answer, so they are an anagram

explanation.surface: Sugary liquids that might give us a burst of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges US SPRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrups are thick liquids of sugar dissolved in water, so they are literally sweet solutions.

clue.text: Change made by video assistant referee? Yes, initially

parts.note: VAR is the football video assistant referee system

indicators.note: initially means just the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Asking whether a football decision was overturned by the video referee, and answering yes.
explanation.walkthrough: VAR is the video replay system used to review decisions in football (soccer).
explanation.definitionFit: To vary is to alter or modify, a verb synonym of change.

clue.text: Dances in series repeated never popular with Charles

indicators.note: repeated means the shortened word is written out twice
never means the word for popular is to be absent from the series

parts.note: a chain is a series of linked things
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Dances in a TV series that keep recurring and were never liked by someone named Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never' strips the popular word from the series to leave CHA, which 'repeated' doubles.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a Latin ballroom dance from Cuba; the plural names several such dances.

clue.text: Section Semite coming into old Italian province

indicators.note: one word comes into the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: Pola, now Pula in Croatia, was an Italian province between the world wars
an Arab is a Semitic person

explanation.surface: A Semitic people entering a former Italian region, like a page of history.
explanation.walkthrough: Pola was the Italian name of Pula, on the Istrian coast, Italian from 1920 to 1947.
explanation.definitionFit: A parabola is a conic section, the curve made by slicing a cone parallel to its side.

clue.text: See 23
See 11
Study as hard after year given 100 pounds to spend?

indicators.note: after places the earlier pieces before the next ones in the answer

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
C is the Roman numeral for 100
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A student cramming after a year, rewarded with a hundred pounds to spend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sets the year and the hundred before the last two pieces; H for hard comes from pencil grading.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready cash is money available immediately, which is what pounds to spend are.

clue.text: Excuse in court excellent defending one bishop on line

indicators.note: the outer word defends what it surrounds, guarding it inside

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI with the 1 as I

indicators.note: on means placed next to the line in this across answer

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A top lawyer defending a bishop accused of something, in a courtroom drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defending' puts L, I and B inside AI.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defendant's plea of having been elsewhere when the crime happened.

clue.text: Bluish ground shields railway next to evil 23 mound

indicators.note: the rearranged letters shield the railway by surrounding it
ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ill can mean evil, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A bluish ground around a railway line beside a sinister prehistoric mound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' makes SILBUH, which 'shields' wraps round the railway. The 23 is the cross-reference to the linked answer AVEBURY STONE CIRCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Silbury Hill is a huge prehistoric artificial mound close to the Avebury monument in Wiltshire.

clue.text: Accident close to fatal in church area

parts.note: chance means accident, an unplanned event

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A fatal accident happening inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' takes the final L of fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar, reserved for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Comes up against objection when giving coverage

indicators.note: the outer word gives coverage by wrapping round the inner one

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Someone meeting an objection while covering a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving coverage' says the word for when wraps round the objection.
explanation.definitionFit: If something abuts another thing it borders it, touching it directly, so it comes up against it.

clue.text: Very old man needing time to follow a TV show

indicators.note: to follow places the later pieces after the a in the answer

parts.note: so can mean very, as in 'so good'
pop is an informal word for father, an old man
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A very old man who needs time to keep up with a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' puts the old man and the time after the a; 'Very old man' reads as one phrase but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama on television about everyday lives.

clue.text: Broadcast international, shooting unknown player?

parts.note: to screen a programme is to broadcast it
a Test is an international match in cricket or rugby

explanation.surface: A broadcast international match where an unknown player was shot down.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket or rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen test is a filmed audition, shooting footage of an untried actor to judge their suitability.

clue.text: Revelation in ballad shortly penned by a writer

indicators.note: penned by means held inside the writing, like an animal in a pen

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a calypso is a Caribbean ballad

explanation.surface: A revelation tucked into a short ballad written by some author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the ballad's final letter and 'penned by' sets what is left inside A and the American writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Apocalypse comes from Greek for uncovering, and the Book of Revelation is also called the Apocalypse.

clue.text: Military event ought to tire band in formation

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a new formation, like soldiers on parade

explanation.surface: A military band that should be tired from marching in formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in formation' rearranges OUGHT TO TIRE BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edinburgh Tattoo is an annual Scottish display of military bands held at Edinburgh Castle.

clue.text: Leader that was Zulu embraced by elevated Archdeacon Basil?

indicators.note: the letter is embraced, held inside the reversed words
elevated in a down clue means read upwards, so the words are reversed

parts.note: Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
basil is a herb
Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A former leader of the Zulus held by a promoted archdeacon named Basil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' makes BREHNEV and 'embraced by' sets the Zulu letter inside it. 'Basil' looks like a name but is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonid Brezhnev was the Soviet Union's leader from 1964 until his death in 1982.

clue.text: Tiny pop star needing dollar also heard in Mali city

parts.note: Tiny Tim was an American pop singer

indicators.note: heard means the words as spoken aloud supply the letters

parts.note: a buck is a dollar and too means also

explanation.surface: A small pop star who needs a dollar too, heard performing in Mali.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiny Tim was a 1960s singer known for 'Tiptoe Through the Tulips'.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbuktu is a historic trading city on the edge of the Sahara in Mali.

clue.text: Back injury — ending for female's mum?

indicators.note: back means the word is written backwards

parts.note: a lesion is an injury to tissue
-ess is the suffix used to make female words, like lioness

explanation.surface: A back injury, and the mother of a woman in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns LESION into NOISEL. 'mum' looks like mother but means silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum as an adjective means silent, as in 'keep mum', and noiseless means making no sound.

clue.text: Poseidon banishing east and north winds to find 1

indicators.note: winds means twists, so the letters are turned about
banishing means sending away these letters from the god's name

explanation.surface: The sea god driving away the east and north winds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banishing' removes E and N from POSEIDON leaving POSIDO, which 'winds' rearranges. 1 refers to CRUSTACEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An isopod is a crustacean of the order Isopoda, such as the woodlouse.

clue.text: Mike entering unconscious state — this gives pause

indicators.note: the letter enters the other word, going inside it

parts.note: a coma is a deep unconscious state
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Mike falling into a coma, which stops things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts M inside COMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma is the punctuation mark that marks a short break when reading.

clue.text: Red blubber that woman slices

indicators.note: the pronoun slices into the other word, ending up inside it

parts.note: to blubber is to cry noisily
her means that woman

explanation.surface: A woman slicing up red whale fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slices' sets the pronoun inside; 'blubber' is the verb to weep, not whale fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry is a bright shade of red, named after the fruit.

clue.text: Forecaster to make gain according to report

indicators.note: according to report means as heard spoken aloud

parts.note: to profit is to make a gain

explanation.surface: A financial forecaster tipped to make a gain, according to a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'according to report' sounds PROFIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet predicts the future, so is a forecaster.

clue.text: Contribute online column

definitions.meaning: to put a message up on a website or social media

explanation.surface: A columnist contributing their work online.
explanation.definitionFit: Post covers both an online message posted and a standing pole, two senses of one word.

clue.text: Buy liver and consecrate for cooking in henge

indicators.note: the letters are cooked, mixed up into a new dish

explanation.surface: Buying liver and blessing it before cooking, at a prehistoric site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cooking' rearranges BUY LIVER and CONSECRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Avebury in Wiltshire is a Neolithic henge, a ditch and bank ringing the largest stone circle in Britain.

clue.text: Composer William has no tips for singer

indicators.note: having no tips means both its end letters are cut off

parts.note: Sir William Walton was an English composer

explanation.surface: A composer called William who never gives tips to singers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no tips' removes W and N from WALTON.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice.

clue.text: See 23
Rudely treat us as soaks

indicators.note: rudely means roughly, so the letters are handled roughly and rearranged

explanation.surface: Drunks who are rude to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rudely' rearranges TREAT US AS. 'soaks' could be a noun for drunks; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To saturate is to drench or wet thoroughly, so saturates means soaks.
